success_patterns: Missing mandatory args are handled with one short seek_information call and nothing else. This happened for a restaurant request with no city, a one-way flight with no departure date, and a hotel request with no check-in or check-out dates. Context such as 'birthday', 'family reunion' or 'family with kids' was not treated as a missing value.

A refinement turn is handled with the load -> filter -> save pattern, loading the right cache key and passing only the new constraint. Examples: a restaurant 'Indonesian, at least 4.5' -> cuisine=['Indonesian'], rating=[4.5, 5]; a hotel 'around 35 per night, business center' -> budget=35, has_business_center=True; a party-size reply -> num_rooms=3, num_people=3 on the hotel key only.
A shared flight preference ('AN in first') is applied to BOTH cached legs, each with its own load, filter and save under a new key.
Restaurant and hotel domains are routed independently. A restaurant answer filters only the restaurants key, even when hotel keys are also cached.
Every search or filter result is assigned to a variable and followed by save_to_cache, with no imports, no loops and no result access.

patch.reasoning: All eight successful trajectories follow behaviours that Rules 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 17, 21 and 22 already encode. These are seek-only turns for missing mandatory args, single-domain filter refinements that pass only the new constraint, a both-legs flight filter, hotel-only filtering for room and people counts, and the straight-line load/filter/save form. The slight deviations (an extra unrelated cache load, a re-search on a 'no preference' turn, different variable or key names) still passed, so they are not patterns worth encoding. No new generalizable pattern is missing from the skill, so no edits are proposed.
